evidence.quote: Mosby Monroe Parsons ( May 21 , 1822 – August 15 , 1865 )
Mosby Monroe Parsons was born in Charlottesville , Virginia

events.text: Family moved to Cole County, Missouri, when he was 13.

evidence.quote: When he was 13 , his parents moved to Cole County , Missouri

events.text: Moved to Jefferson City, Missouri, his home thereafter.

evidence.quote: Two years later , they moved again to Jefferson City , which Parsons would thereafter make his home

events.label: bar admission
events.text: Admitted to the bar after reading law.

evidence.quote: As a young man , Mosby read law and was admitted to the bar in 1846

events.label: military action
events.text: Cited for gallantry at the Battle of Sacramento.

evidence.quote: at the Battle of Sacramento on February 28 , 1847
was cited for gallantry
Parsons married Mary Wells on September 18 , 1850

events.text: Wife Mary Wells died about three years after the marriage.

evidence.quote: However , his wife died just three years later

events.text: Elected to the Missouri state legislature.

evidence.quote: In 1856 was elected to the state legislature

events.text: Became Missouri state senator, serving until the Civil War.

evidence.quote: He became a Missouri state senator in 1858

events.text: Commissioned brigadier general of the Confederacy.

evidence.quote: commissioned a brigadier general of the Confederacy on November 5 , 1862

events.label: battle
events.text: Led his infantry brigade at Prairie Grove, Arkansas.

evidence.quote: led his infantry brigade in the Battle of Prairie Grove , Arkansas , one month later

events.label: battle
events.text: His brigade participated in the attack at Helena, Arkansas.

evidence.quote: His force would participate in the attack at Helena , Arkansas on July 4 , 1863

events.label: battle
events.text: Assisted Richard Taylor against Banks in the Red River Campaign (Pleasant Hill).

evidence.quote: assisted Richard Taylor in thwarting Union Major General Nathaniel Banks Red River Campaign of 1864

events.text: Appointed major general by Kirby Smith; never confirmed by Davis.

evidence.quote: a major general by Trans-Mississippi Departmental Commander Kirby Smith on April 30 , 1864

events.label: death
events.text: Murdered by Captain Dario Garza near China, Nuevo León, Mexico.

evidence.quote: Parsons was murdered by Captain Dario Garza , at the head of a body of Mexican soldiers , on or about August 15 , 1865
were murdered by Captain Dario Garza , at the head of a body of Mexican soldiers , on or about August 15 , 1865

events.label: claim
events.text: Son and sister sued the Mexican government over his murder.

evidence.quote: In 1868 , Parsons son ( Kearny Parsons ) and sister ( Mildred Standish )

events.label: claim
events.text: Claimants awarded judgment of about US$50,000 in gold each.

evidence.quote: In 1875 , a judgment in the amount of almost US$50,000.00 in gold was awarded

undated_mentions: Appointed brigadier general commanding the Sixth Division, Missouri State Guard
Led his division at Carthage and the Battle of Wilsons Creek
Served as a volunteer captain in the Mexican–American War
Served as United States District Attorney for western Missouri
Opposed Steele's Camden Expedition and took part in the Battle of Jenkins Ferry
